description:
USER question (s495, 2026-09-21): "+20.8 %?  Do you mean that the map change made it slower?"  -- YES, and re-measured by Fable because the agent's number existed only as a sentence (no log on disk).
MEASURED (s495, quiet box, load ~1.1; best of 5, startup subtracted; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/probes/mapbench/{multi,single,time}.pl + result-60000.txt; base = 99868bb1, main = 5423c3a9 = with s492b's #2005):
    multi   `my @p = map { ($_, $_ * 2) } 1 .. 200;`  x 60000     base 1.177 s   main 1.405 s   = +19.4 %     perl 0.640 s   (PCL 1.84x perl -> 2.20x perl)
    single  `my @p = map { $_ * 2 } 1 .. 400;`        x 60000     base 1.265 s   main 1.267 s   = unchanged   perl 0.947 s
So the cost is ONLY on a map whose block returns TWO OR MORE elements; the one-element arm always copied and did not move.  No bench-exec row has such a map in its hot loop, so the speed table did not move -- but `map { $_ => f($_) }` (building a hash) is one of the most common everyday shapes, and on it PCL is now 2.2x perl in ABSOLUTE time (USER Target A).
WHY IT IS SLOWER: #2005 fixed a SILENT WRONG (`my %idx = map { $_ => ++$i } qw(a b c)` gave every key the FINAL $i, because the multi-element arm stored the variable's own box).  The fix routes every element of a multi-element result through `%p-map-copy-scalar` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp), which for a plain scalar box ALLOCATES a new box: `(make-p-box (unbox r))`.  The fix is right; "inherent" (the agent's word) is NOT quite right:
  (1) perl's pp_mapwhile copies a value UNLESS IT IS A TEMP -- `$_ * 2`, a literal, a call's result are temps and are NOT copied; only a variable / element (`$_`, `$i`, `++$i`, `$h{k}`) is.  The compiler KNOWS this per result position at compile time (an arithmetic / call / literal leaf cannot be a variable's box).
  (2) since boxed-aggregates phase shipped, array elements are RAW by default: if the map's result is headed for an aggregate or a list assignment, the snapshot the consumer needs may be `(unbox r)` itself -- the fresh box is allocated and then immediately unboxed again.  MEASURE whether that is what happens (allocation profile of multi.pl: count make-p-box calls per iteration, and where the collector's output goes).
LEVERS TO MEASURE, cheapest first: (a) in the collector, snapshot a plain scalar box with `unbox` instead of a fresh box where the consumer stores raw -- probe the BREAKING cases first: `for (map { $_ } @a) { $_ = 0 }` must not write through to @a AND must still be assignable, `map { \$_ } @a` keeps the reference to the ELEMENT, `my @r = map { $x } 1..3; $x = 9` (r2005.pl in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s495/review/s492b/ is the 28-row table -- every row must stay identical to perl); (b) a compile-time per-position "cannot be a variable's box" verdict (a Kind-A gate in Pl/Passes.pm) so temps skip the helper call altogether; (c) the same question for the ONE-element arm, which has paid this since it was written (single is 1.34x perl).
BAR: perf lever => bench A/B with load recorded, r2005.pl identical to perl on base and tree, the four #2005 guard rows in Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t, full sweep (cl/ change), gen bump if (b).  WHERE IT GOES: the perf slot -- a member of, or the round after, s494p (#2098 quadratic `.=`/shift).


=== MEASURED IN s494p (Opus, 2026-09-25/26; perf round 35, member 1's control set) — member 5 NOT taken ===
The two #2198 shapes are now bench-exec ROWS (`mapmulti` = `my @p = map { ($_, $_ * 2) } 1 .. 200` x 60000, `mapsingle` = `my @p = map { $_ * 2 } 1 .. 400` x 60000), verified against perl by the tool, so the board sees them from now on.  Readings on the s494p tree (runtime-only change for map; the map code path is untouched by s494p), best-of-5, startup subtracted:
    mapmulti    perl 0.6315-0.6812 s   PCL 1.3847-1.4772 s   2.17-2.30x perl     (logs scratch/s494p/m4-control-pair.log, m4-boxset-snapshot-ab.log, bars-new-bench-rows.log: 2.18x)
    mapsingle   perl 0.9223-0.9950 s   PCL 1.2176-1.3166 s   1.31-1.37x perl
So s495's measurement (multi 2.20x, single 1.34x) reproduces.  One A/B of the s494p runtime against the 3e8bff3e runtime read both rows -10 % (bars-runtime-ab.log) and a K=7 re-run read -0.7 / +0.5 % — i.e. that first reading was CORE LAYOUT noise, not a lever (s494p changes nothing on the map path).  The levers (a)/(b)/(c) above are untouched; the rows are the bar.
=== DONE (s499f) ===
SHIPPED as commit "s499f M3 (#2198)" (runtime-only).  %p-map-copy-scalar parks a plain number or string RAW (%p-storable-raw) instead of in a fresh box; undef, a dualvar and magic/tied cells keep the fresh box.  The #2005 reproducer and 28 aliasing shapes (probes r2005.pl) print perl's output.  Lever (b), the compile-time per-position licence, was NOT built: the runtime lever alone pays the regression back.
SIZED: mapmulti micro 1.422 -> 1.152 s (-19.0 %); everyday `%h = map { $_ => f($_) }' 200k x5 0.452 -> 0.355 s (-21.4 %); Perfect-shuffle 0.718 -> 0.630 s (-12.2 %).
WHOLE TREE vs e51abda1: bench mapmulti 1.397 -> 1.127 s (-19.3 %; pre-#2005 was 1.177 s -- regression FULLY paid back), mapsingle +0.8 % (noise); Perfect-shuffle -11.9 %, everyday map-hash -18.8 %.
Guard Pl/t/perf-levers-06.t rows 84-85 (mechanism, FAIL on the base) + answer rows.
subject: PERF (regression measured s495, from the #2005 correctness fix): a `map` whose block returns 2+ elements is +19.4 % slower (1.177 -> 1.405 s; perl 0.640 s) -- every element now gets a freshly ALLOCATED box; perl copies only non-TEMPs, and with raw elements the box may be unboxed again at once: measure, then copy less
